measurementKind: Attribution of unchanged product behavior; no optimization applied
conditions: Each desktop run uses an isolated profile/endpoints and real OSS main/preload/renderer/IPC/daemon/MCP. A custom-command Provider launches the actual production Codex ACP bundle and pinned native runtime. Only model Responses API and external provider wire are synthetic loopback fixtures.

Short completed replies, no requested model tools; Home after each Session. Default Session retention unchanged. No tracing/allocation sampling. Explicit main/renderer GC precedes desktop process measurements.
Group footprints are footprint -j total footprint bytes. RSS sums include shared mappings. Separately sampled process groups are not guaranteed to sum exactly.

Standalone ACP samples use explicit signal/sequence acknowledgements to collect adapter GC before measurements. Multiple logical Sessions in one ACP/native pair are a protocol diagnostic; no production pooling, account isolation or failure-fanout equivalence is established.

Goal benchmark invokes the real MessageHandler.hasActiveGoal against an actual persisted Roost SessionDocument and backend, providing its document/backend ports directly. The full MessageHandler and GC timer are not constructed.

Goal benchmark keeps the existing CLI runtime entries and adds a temporary diagnostic entry under the production Vite configuration, runs in actual Electron-as-Node, and resolves the staged native runtime dependencies. Fixture bodies are synthetic low-repetition ASCII text, 128 turns of 1 MiB each.

Goal opened checkpoint follows readHistoryCount. Every checkpoint records ambient process.memoryUsage before explicit GC, then post-GC memory and native footprint. Ambient values are snapshots at call completion, not sampled peak or retained memory. These are standalone owner-process values, not a complete desktop total.
No provider auth, user data or transcripts are included. All controlled desktop and ACP process groups close; owner probes await document/repo shutdown and exit.

goalQueryImplementation.change: Local latest-goal query; Roost fallback bypasses body-cache admission and reuses the existing in-memory goal projection after version validation
goalQueryImplementation.baseline: Same production bundle with local goal capability hidden, executing the previous MessageHandler full-read branch
conditions: Each variant runs in a fresh Electron-as-Node process, production CLI Vite entries retained, same staged native dependencies.

Roost uses independent copies of identical persisted synthetic fixtures. The missing-index variant corrupts only the derived goal index before opening. Recent goals are recovered by ordinary latest-window loading; old-goal/no-goal variants actually traverse four pages on their first query.
Loro creates identical loaded CRDT history in each process. Its preparation time includes fixture construction, not disk opening.
Opening/preparation precedes the first checkpoint; query increments are separate. Each checkpoint collects explicit GC after recording ambient JS heap. Return snapshots are not sampled peaks.
Two queries per process; 128 MiB no-goal variants repeat in a second fresh process. Controls vary count and bytes independently.
Footprint is the process total, not live JS heap. No user data or transcripts. All controlled owner probes finish document/repo cleanup and exit.

Counters record SDK active-branch page and full-branch body reads during each query only. Query results populate only the existing idle-owner goal projection at the validated known cursor, not persisted indexes or body caches.

readonlyFallbackCalibration.variant: Earlier read-only fallback without reuse of the existing in-memory goal projection; same 128 MiB no-goal fixture
